note: Comping a Dorian vamp that turns into a ii–V: the chords strummed to the metronome on a strum-along with its pattern, then over drums and bass with the keys left out, so the learner is the only one playing them. The tempo is moves (90 to 110 bpm), named only as {{=bpm}}; the key stays, since chord tokens can't write Am9 and D9, so the chords are named by their letters. Each block has one feel to reach.

exercise.title: Comp for the jam
exercise.why: The same two chords sound like a Dorian vamp while they loop and like a ii–V the moment Gmaj7 follows them, so the last two bars change what the first six meant.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: Am9 and D9 three times round, a bar each, then two bars of Gmaj7. Strum the pattern written in each box.
Practice until the change to Gmaj7 lands on its beat 1 without a gap in the strumming.

tool.pattern: D . D U . U D U

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass, with the chord boxes lit as the bars go by. You are the only one playing the chords. In the vamp, strum only some of the pattern and leave gaps, then strum every stroke when Gmaj7 arrives.
If you lose your place, keep your strumming hand moving and come back in on the next beat 1.
